documents.title: Staging Reference Data Set Documentation (STG-RDS v3.0)

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
sections.text: This document describes the reference data set STG-RDS v3.0, which is used to calibrate and back-test the significant increase in credit risk (SICR) thresholds of the IFRS 9 SICR and Staging model (inventory identifier MDL-09, model version 2.2), and documents the production input data of the staging engine. The scope covers all financial assets measured at amortised cost or at fair value through other comprehensive income, loan commitments and financial guarantee contracts of the Bank N.V., its consumer credit subsidiary and its Belgian branch that are subject to the IFRS 9 impairment requirements, with a gross carrying amount of EUR 186.2 billion and off-balance commitments and guarantees of EUR 21.7 billion at 31 December 2026. The RDS serves the Stage 1 and Stage 2 allocation of performing exposures; Stage 3 exposures and purchased or originated credit-impaired (POCI) assets are identified from the same data but are not part of the calibration population. The document follows the RDS documentation template of Annex A of the Model Documentation Standard (MRM-STD-021 v3.0) and is version-controlled in the controlled document repository under reference DOC-MDL09-RDS. Version 1.0 was reviewed by S. Mulder (Senior Model Developer, not an author of this document) on 1 March 2027 and approved by the model owner, E. van Dijk (Director IFRS 9 Modelling), on 5 March 2027 after the data quality sign-off of 26 February 2027.

sections.heading: Observation period
sections.text: STG-RDS v3.0 contains 44 quarterly reference dates from 31 March 2015 to 31 December 2025, with default outcomes observed over the twelve months following each reference date up to 31 December 2026 and a stage history look-back of six months before each default. The data set contains 88.7 million facility-quarter observations on 3.26 million unique facilities and 1.87 million unique obligors, and 301,420 obligor-level default events after the merging of multiple defaults, affecting 368,950 facilities. By portfolio the default events are: residential mortgages 17,960 (average annual default rate 0.31%), consumer lending 247,300 (1.72%), retail SME 34,850 (1.64%) and corporates 1,310 (0.98%). Financial institutions, sovereigns and debt securities (1,420 facilities, EUR 12.1 billion) are included for stage allocation but, with only 4 default events in the observation period, are not used for threshold calibration. The row counts and default counts reported in this document are produced by the build code tagged v3.0.0 from the frozen RDS version STG-RDS v3.0.

sections.heading: Choice of observation window
sections.text: The window starts on 31 March 2015 because daily days-past-due history is available for all retail systems only from the migration of the arrears administration to the Arrears Management System (AMS) in the fourth quarter of 2014, and ends on 31 December 2025 so that a complete twelve-month outcome window is observed. The eleven-year window covers the recovery years 2015–2019, the COVID-19 period of 2020–2021 including the general payment moratoria, and the 2022–2023 inflation and interest-rate shock, which provides a mix of benign and stressed years for the trade-off between default capture and stage volatility. The window does not contain a severe Dutch housing downturn comparable to 2008–2013; this is recorded as limitation LIM-09-08 in the MDD and addressed through the sensitivity analysis of MDD section 7.5. The consumer credit subsidiary migrated to the CONS-CORE platform in May 2019; its history before migration is mapped to the new product codes through the version-controlled mapping table map_cons_legacy_v4.csv, documented as expert judgement EJ-09-03. Five years of data are the minimum under FIN-STD-200 §11.2, and the eleven years used exceed it for every portfolio.

sections.heading: Target variable and outcome horizon
sections.text: The calibration target is the occurrence of a default under the Bank's definition of default (CR-STD-110) within twelve months after the reference date; for the capture-rate metric the target is extended to whether a facility that defaulted was allocated to Stage 2 at least six months before its date of default. The twelve-month horizon deviates from the lifetime horizon of the SICR criterion, because the staging thresholds compare lifetime PDs but their performance can only be observed on realised defaults; the six-month early-capture target ensures that SICR is identified before an asset becomes credit-impaired rather than at the point of default. The IFRS 9 definition of default equals the prudential definition of CR-STD-110, so that the target variable is consistent with the definition used for internal credit risk management and Stage 3 comprises all exposures in default under that definition. POCI assets are identified separately by the flag POCI_IND set at purchase or origination and remain outside the Stage 1/Stage 2 calibration population for their whole life.

sections.heading: Deviations from the Bank's definition of default
sections.text: For reference dates from 1 January 2016 onwards, the default flag in STG-RDS v3.0 is taken from the production default register maintained under CR-STD-110 and contains no deviations. For the four reference dates of 2015 the flag is approximated from daily arrears and restructuring data, as described in section 3.3.4. During the general payment moratoria of 2020 that met the conditions of EBA/GL/2020/02, instalments postponed under the moratoria were not counted as past due, in line with the treatment of instalments suspended by law; the moratoria were not classified as forbearance, and exposures were assessed individually for unlikeliness to pay. The effect of the moratoria on the staging signal is recorded as data deficiency DD-09-05, and the quarters 30 June 2020 to 31 March 2021 are excluded from the calibration objective under expert judgement EJ-09-04.

sections.heading: Past-due criterion and materiality threshold
sections.text: An obligor is in default when a material credit obligation is more than 90 days past due or the obligor is assessed as unlikely to pay, with the materiality threshold set at EUR 100 and 1% for retail exposures and EUR 500 and 1% for non-retail exposures. Any amount of principal, interest or fee not paid on its due date is recognised as a past due credit obligation. The absolute component is compared with the sum of all past due amounts of the obligor, and the relative component is that sum divided by the total on-balance-sheet exposure of the obligor to the Bank and its subsidiaries, excluding equity exposures. The relative component of 1% is the level set by the ECB under Regulation (EU) 2018/1845 (ECB/2018/26); the ECB did not substantiate a different level within the 0% to 2.5% range. The days-past-due counter starts on the first day on which both components are exceeded and restarts at zero when either component is no longer exceeded. Days past due are counted daily in AMS and in the Corporate Loan System (CLS) for all obligors; where the payment schedule is modified, days past due are counted on the modified schedule. Obligations of the Belgian branch denominated in currencies other than the euro are converted at the daily ECB reference rate, and the absolute component is set in euro only, so that no foreign-currency threshold arises. The flag DOD_MAT_REGIME identifies that the regulatory materiality threshold is applied from 31 December 2020, the date of application set by the ECB, and that earlier reference dates use the Bank's previous threshold of EUR 250 without relative component.

sections.heading: Level of application, contagion and date of default
sections.text: Default is identified at obligor level for all exposure classes, including retail, and all credit obligations of a defaulted obligor are flagged as defaulted in every relevant system of the Bank, the consumer credit subsidiary and the Belgian branch. Once the past-due criterion is met, the obligor is classified as defaulted without additional expert judgement. The same definition of default is used for all exposure types across the Bank, its subsidiary and its branch, so that no separate scope of application needs to be specified. Joint credit obligations and contagion between connected clients follow section 8 of EBA/GL/2016/07 as implemented in CR-STD-110 §4.3: the default of an obligor in a group of connected clients triggers a case-by-case assessment of the other group members by Credit Risk Management, and a default on a joint obligation is propagated to individual exposures of the co-obligors only where the joint default is material to them. The date of default is the first day on which any default criterion is met and is stored in DEFAULT_DATE for every default event; where the underlying process runs less often than daily, the date on which the criterion was actually fulfilled is used. Default flags are propagated to all exposures of a defaulted obligor in the source systems within one business day, and the monthly RDS snapshot is taken after propagation so that recording delays do not affect the data used for calibration.

sections.heading: Probation periods and multiple defaults
sections.text: An obligor returns to non-default status only after at least three months without any default trigger and a documented assessment of its behaviour and financial situation confirming that the improvement in credit quality is factual and permanent. After a distressed restructuring the probation period is at least twelve months from the latest of the restructuring measure, the default classification or the end of any grace period, and return requires a material payment, regular payments under the new schedule, no amount past due and no remaining doubt about full repayment. The probation start date and status are stored in PROB_START_DT and PROB_STATUS for every default event. Where an obligor defaults again within twelve months of returning to non-default status, both events are treated as a single default starting on the first date of default; STG-RDS v3.0 links such events through DEFAULT_EVENT_ID and 14,730 events were merged. Probation periods could not be reconstructed for the 2015 reference dates because the UTP and cure history before 2016 is not available at event level; for these dates cure is assumed at the date on which the past-due criterion ceased, as stated in section 3.3.4.

sections.heading: Historical approximation of the default flag
sections.text: For the reference dates of 2015 the default flag is approximated from daily arrears in AMS and CLS combined with the restructuring register, because the default register under the definition of default of EBA/GL/2016/07 was back-filled only from 1 January 2016. The approximation flags a default when the EUR 250 arrears amount was more than 90 days past due or a restructuring with a debt reduction was recorded, and does not capture the other unlikeliness-to-pay triggers. On the overlap year 2016, the approximated flag identifies 97.6% of the register defaults and produces a default rate that is 2.4% lower in relative terms than the register flag, with the difference concentrated in corporate unlikeliness-to-pay defaults. The effect is recorded as data deficiency DD-09-01; because the 2015 reference dates represent 9% of the calibration observations, re-running the threshold calibration without them changes no selected threshold.

sections.heading: Automatic unlikeliness-to-pay triggers
sections.text: The following unlikeliness-to-pay triggers lead to default automatically and are mapped to source fields in the default engine: non-accrued status (NONACCR_IND in the general ledger interface), a specific credit risk adjustment or Stage 3 classification resulting from a significant perceived decline in credit quality, a sale of credit obligations at a credit-related economic loss above 5%, a distressed restructuring with a diminished financial obligation above 1%, bankruptcy or similar protection, and a forced sale of collateral. Exposures classified as credit-impaired (Stage 3) are considered defaulted in all cases, because the Bank does not apply the payment-delay exceptions of paragraph 39 of EBA/GL/2016/07. Collective allowances for incurred-but-not-reported losses and Stage 1 and Stage 2 allowances are not treated as indications of unlikeliness to pay. The credit-related economic loss on a sale is computed as L = (E − P)/E with a threshold of 5%, and the reasons for each sale and its loss are analysed by Financial Restructuring and Recovery before a loss is treated as not credit-related. Where a sale at a material credit-related loss precedes default identification, the date of sale is the date of default. The diminished financial obligation is calculated as (NPV0 − NPV1)/NPV0, with both net present values discounted at the original effective interest rate.

sections.heading: Case-by-case indicators and external information
sections.text: Additional unlikeliness-to-pay indicators defined per exposure type in CR-STD-110 §6.2, such as fraud, a significant decline in income or cash flow, covenant breaches and multiple forbearance, lead to a case-by-case assessment completed by Credit Risk Management within 30 days of detection. Each trigger and indicator is mapped to source-system fields in the UTP mapping table utp_map_v7.csv, and the outcome of every case-by-case assessment is recorded with its rationale in the credit workflow system CWS. For each indicator, the mapping table defines the identification method, the internal and external information sources and the monitoring frequency; external sources include the BKR credit register for retail obligors, the Central Insolvency Register and press and analyst monitoring for corporate obligors. Manual identification processes (watchlist reviews, forbearance lists and external insolvency alerts) are updated at least weekly, and daily for insolvency alerts. UTP triggers and dpd triggers are applied consistently across the Bank, the consumer credit subsidiary and the Belgian branch.

sections.heading: Forbearance and forborne exposures
sections.text: Forbearance flags are taken from the Forbearance Register (FBR) maintained by Credit Risk Management under the definitions of Annex V of Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/451. For every forbearance measure the diminished financial obligation is computed, and forborne exposures below the 1% threshold are assessed for other indications of unlikeliness to pay, including a large final lump-sum payment, a back-loaded or irregular schedule, a significant grace period and repeated forbearance. All exposures classified as forborne non-performing are classified as defaulted, and a quarterly control by Credit Risk Management verifies this and reviews forborne performing exposures for indications of unlikeliness to pay. Forborne performing exposures carry the flag FORB_PERF_IND and the forborne-performing probation end date FORB_PROB_END_DT, which the staging engine uses to keep these exposures in Stage 2 for at least the two-year probation period. Where the schedule is changed as a forbearance measure, the assessment of distressed restructuring is performed before days past due are counted on the modified schedule.

sections.heading: Technical past due
sections.text: Technical past due situations are recognised only in the cases listed in EBA/GL/2016/07, namely errors of the Bank's data or systems, failures of payment execution, time lags in the allocation of payments and the specified factoring cases; wrong credit decisions are never treated as technical past due. Each case is registered in the technical past due log with the IT incident number, corrected within 30 days and reviewed quarterly by Credit Risk Management. Between 2016 and 2025 the log contains 1,184 technical past due cases, of which 1,102 related to the 2019 migration of the consumer credit subsidiary; the corresponding default flags were corrected in the source systems before the RDS snapshot. Technical past due cases do not reset the staging backstop counter used for the 30 days past due criterion, which is based on the same materiality-adjusted counter as the default definition.

sections.heading: Default flag reconciliation and default definition register
sections.text: The default flag constructed in STG-RDS v3.0 was reconciled with the production default register of CR-STD-110 for all reference dates from 31 March 2016 onwards: 99.94% of obligor-level default events agree on flag and date, and the 181 differences are explained by retroactive corrections of default dates in the register after the RDS snapshot. The RDS default flag is constructed in accordance with CR-STD-110, including the materiality thresholds, the unlikeliness-to-pay triggers, the probation periods and the merging of multiple defaults. The default flags used for IRB and IFRS 9 purposes are reconciled quarterly between the risk data warehouse and the Finance Risk Data Platform (FRDP); the reconciliation of 31 December 2026 showed no unexplained difference. Credit Risk Management maintains the register of current and past default definitions, which records for each definition its scope, approving body and date, implementation date and a description of the changes; the register entry DoD-2021-01 records the implementation of EBA/GL/2016/07 and the ECB materiality threshold on 31 December 2020. The accounting definition of default used for Stage 3 is therefore guided by Article 178 CRR and covers both unlikeliness to pay and 90 days past due, with unlikeliness to pay identified before 90 days past due is reached where the triggers of section 3.4 apply.

sections.heading: Source systems and extraction
sections.text: STG-RDS v3.0 is built from monthly snapshots of the Finance Risk Data Platform (FRDP), which is the authoritative source for IFRS 9 input data and is fed by the mortgage administration HYPO-NL, the consumer lending platform CONS-CORE, the Corporate Loan System (CLS), the Arrears Management System (AMS), the Forbearance Register (FBR), the Early Warning and Watchlist system (EWS), the default engine and the IFRS 9 PD term structure store. Snapshots are extracted on the fifth business day after each quarter end, and the source snapshot reference dates of all 44 quarters are listed in section 8. The data set is mapped to the data domains Retail Lending, Corporate Lending, Credit Risk Management and Finance, each of which has one Data Owner recorded in the Group Data Catalogue. The IFRS 9 PD term structures used for the SICR ratio are produced by the IFRS 9 PD models for mortgages (MDL-07), corporates (MDL-08), consumer lending and retail SME, conditional on the macroeconomic scenarios and weights of MDL-10. No third-party data enter the RDS except the BKR registration status, whose lineage starts at the monthly BKR delivery received by the Bank and records the provider, the data product BKR-Toetsing and the delivery date.

sections.heading: Lineage and critical data elements
sections.text: The lineage of every RDS variable, including discarded variables used to construct retained variables, is documented in Annex A and in the Group Data Catalogue, and identifies the source system and fields, each intermediate data store, every transformation, filter, join and aggregation with the reference to the build script or ETL job, and the extraction frequency and timing. Every staging input variable and every data element used to construct the default target (default flag, default date, probation status) is designated as a critical data element; STG-RDS v3.0 contains 23 critical data elements. Each critical data element has a business definition, a technical definition and at least one data quality rule per applicable dimension, recorded in the DQ rule book DQR-STG-v3. The model owner agreed the data quality expectations for the 23 critical data elements with the Data Owners of the four domains in the data sharing agreement DSA-IFRS9-004 of 12 January 2027. Roles for the ownership and quality of the data are defined for business (Data Owners and Data Stewards in Finance and Credit Risk Management) and IT (FRDP platform owner in Finance Risk IT).

sections.heading: Exclusions
sections.text: Six exclusions are applied to the calibration population; none of them removes facilities from production stage allocation. E1 dormant facilities with zero balance and zero available limit: 2.1% of facility-quarters, no default events; E2 POCI assets: 0.02% of observations and 212 default events, excluded because they are not staged; E3 facilities in default at the reference date: 1.6% of observations, excluded because they are not in the performing population. E4 facilities without origination PD and without a feasible proxy: 0.4% of observations and 0.5% of default events; E5 intra-group positions: 0.1% of observations; E6 duplicate facility records created by the 2019 migration of the consumer credit subsidiary: 0.3% of observations, removed under the uniqueness rule. Each exclusion is justified, quantified by number of facilities, share of observations and number of default events, and assessed for its effect on representativeness in section 5.3, which concludes that no exclusion changes the default rate of any portfolio by more than 0.02 percentage points. Exclusion E1 exceeds 5% of observations in the consumer lending segment (6.8%, dormant credit cards) and was approved by the model owner on 26 February 2027 and reported to Model Validation.

sections.heading: Missing values and outliers
sections.text: Missing values are treated per variable as documented in Annex C, distinguishing values missing at random, values missing for a structural reason and values missing because of a data deficiency. The watchlist status is structurally missing for retail obligors outside the scope of the watchlist and is set to "not on watchlist"; missing days past due (0.02% of observations) are recomputed from the daily AMS history, so that no value is imputed statistically. Missing origination PDs of legacy facilities are replaced by the proxy of section 4.4, a documented and reproducible method; the share of proxied values is 14.8% for mortgages, 9.6% for retail SME and 3.1% for corporates, and the effect on the calibrated thresholds is assessed in MDD section 7.5. Outliers of the SICR ratio above 50, caused by the origination PD floor of 0.03%, are identified by a documented rule that is applied identically in the RDS build and the production engine; the ratio is capped at 50 for calibration statistics only, which has no effect on stage allocation because every relative threshold lies below 3.0. Missing values and outliers of the default flag and default date are not imputed; the 38 affected default events were investigated and corrected at source in the default register.

sections.heading: Origination PD and legacy proxy
sections.text: The origination PD term structure, the origination rating and the date of initial recognition are stored for every facility in the FRDP table ORIG_RISK for the full life of the facility and are never overwritten by later recalibrations. For loan commitments and financial guarantee contracts, the date of initial recognition is the date on which the Bank became party to the irrevocable commitment, and the origination PD is stored at that date. For modified financial assets that are not derecognised, ORIG_RISK retains the origination PD of the original, unmodified terms, while a modification with derecognition creates a new facility with a new date of initial recognition. For facilities originated before origination PDs were stored (mortgages before 2008, retail SME before 2012 and corporates before 2010), the origination PD is proxied by the PD of the earliest archived rating, adjusted to the origination date with the portfolio-average rating migration between origination and first rating; the proxy approach is documented as EJ-09-03 and data deficiency DD-09-02. For mortgages, allocating legacy facilities with the alternative proxy (earliest rating without migration adjustment) changes the Stage 2 share of legacy facilities from 7.1% to 7.6%, and the impact on the total loss allowance is EUR 1.9 million.

sections.heading: Staging input variables
sections.text: The staging engine uses days past due at facility level, based on the same materiality-adjusted counter as the definition of default, the forborne performing flag and probation end date from FBR, and the watchlist status from EWS, in addition to the current and origination lifetime PD term structures. The watchlist status is maintained by Credit Risk Management under CR-POL-001 §10.1, whereby obligors triggering an early-warning indicator are assessed within 30 days and placed on the watchlist where deterioration is confirmed; performing exposures of obligors on the watchlist are allocated to Stage 2. Performing exposures more than 30 days past due on a material amount are allocated to Stage 2, and the rebuttable presumption of IFRS 9 is not rebutted for any portfolio. The RDS contains these inputs at each reference date so that the full stage allocation, not only the quantitative criterion, can be replicated and back-tested. The facility grouping variables (portfolio, product, origination PD band, collateral type, origination vintage and remaining term) are stored with each observation so that collective assessment and performance analysis can be performed on groups sharing credit risk characteristics.

sections.heading: Data ownership, metadata and change control
sections.text: Metadata for every RDS variable (business and technical definition, type and format, permitted values, unit and currency, source, Data Owner, update frequency and classification) are recorded in the Group Data Catalogue, using the integrated group taxonomy with the global customer identifier GCID and the facility identifier FAC_ID. The accounting and prudential notions of default are identical under FIN-STD-200 §4.2, but the credit-impaired flag used for Stage 3 (IFRS9_CI_IND) and the prudential default flag (DOD_FLAG) are labelled distinctly and their identity is verified by the quarterly reconciliation of section 3.5. Metadata changes are versioned in the catalogue so that the definition applicable to any historical data point can be retrieved. Changes to the definition, source or transformation logic of a staging input are approved by the Data Owner and announced to the model owner through the FRDP change calendar at least one quarter before implementation. The lineage documentation is updated before changed data are used in development, monitoring or production; the change of the watchlist feed from monthly to daily in March 2026 was reflected in lineage version 3.2 before its first production use.

sections.heading: Manual interventions
sections.text: The RDS build and the production data flow are fully automated, and no manual data manipulation is used in the build; the two unavoidable manual inputs, the legacy product mapping table map_cons_legacy_v4.csv and the UTP mapping table utp_map_v7.csv, are version-controlled files documented as expert judgement EJ-09-03 and as a Credit Risk Management reference table respectively. Manual interventions in the production flow are limited to stage overrides entered in the Staging Override Tool and to the collective Stage 2 transfer list maintained by IFRS 9 Modelling; both are identified in the lineage together with their controls (four-eyes approval in the tool and reconciliation of the transfer list to the Group Impairment Committee decision). Corrections of model data not supported by source evidence are not permitted; the 38 corrections of default dates referred to in section 4.3 were made at source with documented evidence.

sections.heading: Representativeness
sections.text: The representativeness of STG-RDS v3.0 for the portfolio at 31 December 2026 was assessed on the distributions of the staging drivers and on default-rate levels, with the detailed tables in Annex B. The population stability index of the origination PD band distribution between the last calibration year (2025) and the portfolio at 31 December 2026 is 0.03 for mortgages, 0.07 for consumer lending, 0.04 for retail SME and 0.05 for corporates, and the PSI of the SICR ratio distribution lies between 0.04 and 0.08. Observed one-year default rates in 2026 (mortgages 0.29%, consumer lending 1.84%, retail SME 1.60%, corporates 0.39%) lie within the range observed in the calibration window for every portfolio. Qualitatively, the product mix, the underwriting standards and the arrears and collection processes are unchanged except for the consumer credit card limit policy tightened in 2024, which reduces the share of high origination PD facilities. It is concluded that STG-RDS v3.0 is representative of the current portfolio for the purpose of threshold calibration.

sections.heading: Representativeness for other uses
sections.text: The staging model is applied to financial institutions, sovereigns and debt securities, which are not represented in the calibration population because of their very low number of defaults. For these exposures the corporate thresholds are applied, and debt securities with an internal rating equivalent to investment grade use the low credit risk exemption described in MDD section 4.8; the internal rating is primary, and where it is more favourable than the external rating the difference is justified in the credit file. The representativeness of the corporate thresholds for these exposures is assessed qualitatively by comparing the PD ranges: 98% of these exposures have origination PDs within the range covered by the corporate calibration population. This use is recorded as limitation LIM-09-10 in the MDD.

sections.heading: Data quality assessment
sections.text: A documented data quality assessment of STG-RDS v3.0 was performed before the recalibration, against the mandatory dimensions completeness, accuracy, consistency and timeliness and the additional dimensions validity, uniqueness and appropriateness of MRM-STD-022; the results per critical data element are reported in the data quality assessment report EVD-09-DQ. All 23 critical data elements are green on completeness (99.4% to 100% non-missing after structural missing values), and the reconciliation of the gross carrying amount to the general ledger at the four 2025 quarter ends shows differences between 0.03% and 0.08%. Two consistency rules were amber during 2019 (migration of the consumer credit subsidiary) and are explained by data deficiency DD-09-03. The assessment concluded that the data are fit for the calibration and back-testing of the SICR thresholds, and was signed off by the model developer R. Jansen and the model owner E. van Dijk on 26 February 2027 before the RDS was frozen.

sections.heading: Data deficiencies
sections.text: The data deficiency log of MDL-09 contains five open deficiencies: DD-09-01 approximated default flag for 2015, DD-09-02 missing origination PD for legacy facilities, DD-09-03 incomplete forbearance history of the consumer credit subsidiary before May 2019, DD-09-04 monthly watchlist history for retail SME before 2017 and DD-09-05 muted arrears signal during the 2020 payment moratoria. Impact, treatment and the cross-references to the MDD limitations log will be completed after the calibration results are available. The deficiencies will also be registered in the Bank data issue register.

sections.heading: Data quality thresholds
sections.text: The DQ rules for the critical data elements use the default amber and red thresholds of MRM-STD-022 §4.3, except for the default flag, the default date and days past due, for which stricter thresholds apply (amber below 99.5% and red below 99.0% on consistency, and amber above 0.1% and red above 0.25% on reconciliation differences). No threshold is less strict than the defaults, so no deviation required approval under MRM-STD-022 §4.5; the stricter thresholds were approved by the model owner together with this document. The DQ rules are documented in the DQ rule book DQR-STG-v3, and the 41 recurring checks are implemented in the Group DQ monitoring tool with a monthly run on the production input data. Red threshold breaches on a critical data element of the staging model are escalated to Model Risk Management within ten business days and reported to the Model Risk Committee.

sections.heading: Data quality of production input data
sections.text: The DQ rules applied to STG-RDS v3.0 are applied unchanged to the monthly production input data of the staging engine, so that production data quality can be compared with the development data. Production runs are blocked when the completeness check on current PDs, days past due or default flags is red, and the fallback rule then allocates facilities without a current PD to Stage 2 until the data are corrected. The input data are reconciled to the general ledger at each quarterly reporting date, and the gross carrying amount difference at 31 December 2026 was 0.04%, below the Finance materiality threshold. The staging output is available on the third business day after month end, which meets the Finance closing timetable for quarterly and monthly reporting; during the 2020 stress period the same timetable was met.

sections.heading: Lawful basis and purposes
sections.text: The staging model processes personal data of natural persons (retail mortgage and consumer lending customers and sole proprietors in retail SME) for three purposes recorded in the Record of Processing: calibration and development, independent validation, and monthly production stage allocation for financial reporting. Production stage allocation is based on Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR, the legal obligation to prepare financial statements under the IAS Regulation (EC) No 1606/2002 and Book 2 of the Dutch Civil Code, and development and validation are based on Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR, with the legitimate interest assessment LIA-2024-033 documenting purpose, necessity and the balancing against data subjects' rights. The lawful bases were recorded before processing started, in the Record of Processing entry ROPA-FIN-0147 of 11 March 2024. The reuse of loan administration data, collected for contract execution, for model development was assessed as compatible under Art. 6(4) GDPR in the compatibility assessment CA-2024-019, which considers the link between purposes, the context of collection, the nature of the data, the possible consequences for data subjects and the pseudonymisation applied. sections.heading: Data minimisation, pseudonymisation and security
sections.text: STG-RDS v3.0 contains the following personal data attributes: pseudonymised obligor token, facility identifier, product and origination date, contractual maturity, gross carrying amount and limit, PD term structures, days past due and arrears amount, forbearance flag and reason category, watchlist status and default flag and date; each attribute is justified by its role in stage allocation or in the calibration target in Annex A. Name, address, date of birth, postcode, income and nationality are not extracted, so that personal data use is limited to what is necessary for stage allocation. Direct identifiers are replaced by keyed HMAC-SHA256 tokens in the FRDP extraction layer, with the keys held by the Group Data Office as separate data custodian; re-identification is possible only for a Privacy Office-approved purpose and is logged, and no re-identification took place for this RDS. The RDS is held only in the secure analytics environment SAE-RISK with role-based access for the eleven named members of IFRS 9 Modelling and Model Validation, encryption at rest and access logging. Implementation testing uses the pseudonymised RDS extract, not identifiable production data.

sections.heading: Protected attributes and fair treatment
sections.text: No protected attributes (such as gender, ethnic origin, nationality or religion) and no age variable are used in the staging model or its calibration. Special categories of personal data are not processed: the forbearance reason code "illness or disability" in FBR is mapped to the generic category "income loss" in the extraction layer, so that no health data enter the RDS. The staging inputs are PDs, arrears, forbearance and watchlist status; proxy screening against postcode-level and age-related information, performed for the IFRS 9 PD models, found no staging input that acts as a proxy for a protected attribute, and the results are documented in the RDS documentation of those PD models and summarised here.

sections.heading: Reproducibility
sections.text: The RDS build code is held in the repository ifrs9/stg-rds-build and STG-RDS v3.0 was produced from tag v3.0.0-rc2 with the source snapshot reference dates 31 March 2015 to 31 December 2025 and outcome snapshots up to 31 December 2026. The software environment is Python 3.11.8 with pandas 2.2.1 and PySpark 3.5.1. The full rebuild from source will be performed after the tag is finalised and its result will be added to this chapter.

sections.heading: Data dictionary
sections.text: Annex A lists for each of the 64 RDS variables its business definition, source system and field, transformation and lineage reference. Examples of the 23 critical data elements: DPD_MAT (days past due on the materiality-adjusted counter; AMS.DPD_CNT and CLS.PD_DAYS; maximum over the facility's instalments, reset per RTS 2018/171), PD_LT_CUR and PD_LT_ORIG (annualised remaining lifetime PD at reporting date and at origination for the same remaining term; PD term structure store; probability-weighted over the MDL-10 scenarios), FORB_PERF_IND (FBR.FORB_STATUS = 'FP'), WL_IND (EWS.WL_STATUS in 'WATCH','ENHANCED'), DOD_FLAG and DEFAULT_DATE (default engine), and GCA (FRDP.GROSS_CARRYING_AMT, reconciled to the general ledger). For every variable the Data Owner, update frequency and data classification are taken from the Group Data Catalogue.

sections.heading: Lineage of key variables
sections.text: The lineage of PD_LT_ORIG runs from the PD term structure store (table PDTS_ORIG, written once at initial recognition by the IFRS 9 PD engine) through the FRDP staging layer (job FRDP_STG_017) to the RDS build script build/orig_risk.py, which annualises the remaining-lifetime PD for the remaining term at each reference date. The lineage of DPD_MAT runs from the daily AMS and CLS arrears tables through the default engine counter (job DOD_DPD_001) to the FRDP facility snapshot and build/arrears.py, with no manual step. The lineage of the development data was compared with the lineage of the production input data of the staging engine; both read the same FRDP tables, and the only difference is the legacy product mapping, which is applied in the RDS build but is no longer needed in production.

sections.heading: Representativeness analyses
sections.text: Annex B contains, per portfolio, the distribution of observations over origination PD bands for each calibration year and for 31 December 2026, the PSI per band, the distribution of the SICR ratio, and the observed default rates per year compared with the current year. For consumer lending, the share of facilities in the highest origination PD band (at least 3%) fell from 21.4% in 2019 to 16.8% at 31 December 2026, reflecting the tightened credit card limit policy; the PSI of 0.07 remains green. Default rates per origination PD band in 2026 lie within the minimum and maximum annual rates of the calibration window for all 11 band-portfolio combinations, so that representativeness also holds on default-rate levels.

sections.heading: Missing values and outliers per variable
sections.text: Annex C lists for each variable the share of missing values, the missingness type and the treatment: DPD_MAT 0.02% missing due to a data deficiency, recomputed from daily history; WL_IND 71.3% structurally missing (retail outside watchlist scope), set to zero; PD_LT_ORIG 11.6% missing for legacy facilities, proxied under EJ-09-03; FORB_REASON 0.4% missing at random, set to "unknown" without effect on staging. Outlier rules are defined for GCA (negative values, investigated and corrected at source), the SICR ratio (above 50, capped for statistics only) and the remaining term (above 40 years, verified against contracts; 312 mortgage facilities with extension options confirmed). The impact of the ratio cap on the calibration statistics is nil, because all thresholds lie below the cap.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
sections.text: This document describes the reference data set STG-RDS v3.0, which is used to calibrate and back-test the significant increase in credit risk (SICR) thresholds of the IFRS 9 SICR and Staging model (inventory identifier MDL-09, model version 2.2), and documents the production input data of the staging engine. The scope covers all financial assets measured at amortised cost or at fair value through other comprehensive income, loan commitments and financial guarantee contracts of the Bank N.V., its consumer credit subsidiary and its Belgian branch that are subject to the IFRS 9 impairment requirements, with a gross carrying amount of EUR 186.2 billion and off-balance commitments and guarantees of EUR 21.7 billion at 31 December 2026. The RDS serves the Stage 1 and Stage 2 allocation of performing exposures; Stage 3 exposures and purchased or originated credit-impaired (POCI) assets are identified from the same data but are not part of the calibration population. The document follows the RDS documentation template of Annex A of the Model Documentation Standard (MRM-STD-021 v3.0) and is version-controlled in the controlled document repository under reference DOC-MDL09-RDS. Version 1.0 was reviewed by S. Mulder (Senior Model Developer, not an author of this document) on 1 March 2027 and approved by the model owner, E. van Dijk (Director IFRS 9 Modelling), on 5 March 2027 after the data quality sign-off of 26 February 2027.

sections.heading: Observation period
sections.text: STG-RDS v3.0 contains 44 quarterly reference dates from 31 March 2015 to 31 December 2025, with default outcomes observed over the twelve months following each reference date up to 31 December 2026 and a stage history look-back of six months before each default. The data set contains 88.7 million facility-quarter observations on 3.26 million unique facilities and 1.87 million unique obligors, and 301,420 obligor-level default events after the merging of multiple defaults, affecting 368,950 facilities. By portfolio the default events are: residential mortgages 17,960 (average annual default rate 0.31%), consumer lending 247,300 (1.72%), retail SME 34,850 (1.64%) and corporates 1,310 (0.98%). Financial institutions, sovereigns and debt securities (1,420 facilities, EUR 12.1 billion) are included for stage allocation but, with only 4 default events in the observation period, are not used for threshold calibration. The row counts and default counts reported in this document are produced by the build code tagged v3.0.0 from the frozen RDS version STG-RDS v3.0.

evidence.quote: STG-RDS v3.0 contains 44 quarterly reference dates from 31 March 2015 to 31 December 2025, with default outcomes observed over the twelve months following each reference date up to 31 December 2026 and a stage history look-back of six months before each default.

sections.heading: Choice of observation window
sections.text: The window starts on 31 March 2015 because daily days-past-due history is available for all retail systems only from the migration of the arrears administration to the Arrears Management System (AMS) in the fourth quarter of 2014, and ends on 31 December 2025 so that a complete twelve-month outcome window is observed. The eleven-year window covers the recovery years 2015–2019, the COVID-19 period of 2020–2021 including the general payment moratoria, and the 2022–2023 inflation and interest-rate shock, which provides a mix of benign and stressed years for the trade-off between default capture and stage volatility. The window does not contain a severe Dutch housing downturn comparable to 2008–2013; this is recorded as limitation LIM-09-08 in the MDD and addressed through the sensitivity analysis of MDD section 7.5. The consumer credit subsidiary migrated to the CONS-CORE platform in May 2019; its history before migration is mapped to the new product codes through the version-controlled mapping table map_cons_legacy_v4.csv, documented as expert judgement EJ-09-03. Five years of data are the minimum under FIN-STD-200 §11.2, and the eleven years used exceed it for every portfolio.

sections.heading: Target variable and outcome horizon
sections.text: The calibration target is the occurrence of a default under the Bank's definition of default (CR-STD-110) within twelve months after the reference date; for the capture-rate metric the target is extended to whether a facility that defaulted was allocated to Stage 2 at least six months before its date of default. The twelve-month horizon deviates from the lifetime horizon of the SICR criterion, because the staging thresholds compare lifetime PDs but their performance can only be observed on realised defaults; the six-month early-capture target ensures that SICR is identified before an asset becomes credit-impaired rather than at the point of default. The IFRS 9 definition of default equals the prudential definition of CR-STD-110, so that the target variable is consistent with the definition used for internal credit risk management and Stage 3 comprises all exposures in default under that definition. POCI assets are identified separately by the flag POCI_IND set at purchase or origination and remain outside the Stage 1/Stage 2 calibration population for their whole life.

sections.heading: Deviations from the Bank's definition of default
sections.text: For reference dates from 1 January 2016 onwards, the default flag in STG-RDS v3.0 is taken from the production default register maintained under CR-STD-110 and contains no deviations. For the four reference dates of 2015 the flag is approximated from daily arrears and restructuring data, as described in section 3.3.4. During the general payment moratoria of 2020 that met the conditions of EBA/GL/2020/02, instalments postponed under the moratoria were not counted as past due, in line with the treatment of instalments suspended by law; the moratoria were not classified as forbearance, and exposures were assessed individually for unlikeliness to pay. The effect of the moratoria on the staging signal is recorded as data deficiency DD-09-05, and the quarters 30 June 2020 to 31 March 2021 are excluded from the calibration objective under expert judgement EJ-09-04.

sections.heading: Past-due criterion and materiality threshold
sections.text: An obligor is in default when a material credit obligation is more than 90 days past due or the obligor is assessed as unlikely to pay, with the materiality threshold set at EUR 100 and 1% for retail exposures and EUR 500 and 1% for non-retail exposures. Any amount of principal, interest or fee not paid on its due date is recognised as a past due credit obligation. The absolute component is compared with the sum of all past due amounts of the obligor, and the relative component is that sum divided by the total on-balance-sheet exposure of the obligor to the Bank and its subsidiaries, excluding equity exposures. The relative component of 1% is the level set by the ECB under Regulation (EU) 2018/1845 (ECB/2018/26); the ECB did not substantiate a different level within the 0% to 2.5% range. The days-past-due counter starts on the first day on which both components are exceeded and restarts at zero when either component is no longer exceeded. Days past due are counted daily in AMS and in the Corporate Loan System (CLS) for all obligors; where the payment schedule is modified, days past due are counted on the modified schedule. Obligations of the Belgian branch denominated in currencies other than the euro are converted at the daily ECB reference rate, and the absolute component is set in euro only, so that no foreign-currency threshold arises. The flag DOD_MAT_REGIME identifies that the regulatory materiality threshold is applied from 31 December 2020, the date of application set by the ECB, and that earlier reference dates use the Bank's previous threshold of EUR 250 without relative component.

sections.heading: Level of application, contagion and date of default
sections.text: Default is identified at obligor level for all exposure classes, including retail, and all credit obligations of a defaulted obligor are flagged as defaulted in every relevant system of the Bank, the consumer credit subsidiary and the Belgian branch. Once the past-due criterion is met, the obligor is classified as defaulted without additional expert judgement. The same definition of default is used for all exposure types across the Bank, its subsidiary and its branch, so that no separate scope of application needs to be specified. Joint credit obligations and contagion between connected clients follow section 8 of EBA/GL/2016/07 as implemented in CR-STD-110 §4.3: the default of an obligor in a group of connected clients triggers a case-by-case assessment of the other group members by Credit Risk Management, and a default on a joint obligation is propagated to individual exposures of the co-obligors only where the joint default is material to them. The date of default is the first day on which any default criterion is met and is stored in DEFAULT_DATE for every default event; where the underlying process runs less often than daily, the date on which the criterion was actually fulfilled is used. Default flags are propagated to all exposures of a defaulted obligor in the source systems within one business day, and the monthly RDS snapshot is taken after propagation so that recording delays do not affect the data used for calibration.

sections.heading: Probation periods and multiple defaults
sections.text: An obligor returns to non-default status only after at least three months without any default trigger and a documented assessment of its behaviour and financial situation confirming that the improvement in credit quality is factual and permanent. After a distressed restructuring the probation period is at least twelve months from the latest of the restructuring measure, the default classification or the end of any grace period, and return requires a material payment, regular payments under the new schedule, no amount past due and no remaining doubt about full repayment. The probation start date and status are stored in PROB_START_DT and PROB_STATUS for every default event. Where an obligor defaults again within twelve months of returning to non-default status, both events are treated as a single default starting on the first date of default; STG-RDS v3.0 links such events through DEFAULT_EVENT_ID and 14,730 events were merged. Probation periods could not be reconstructed for the 2015 reference dates because the UTP and cure history before 2016 is not available at event level; for these dates cure is assumed at the date on which the past-due criterion ceased, as stated in section 3.3.4.

sections.heading: Historical approximation of the default flag
sections.text: For the reference dates of 2015 the default flag is approximated from daily arrears in AMS and CLS combined with the restructuring register, because the default register under the definition of default of EBA/GL/2016/07 was back-filled only from 1 January 2016. The approximation flags a default when the EUR 250 arrears amount was more than 90 days past due or a restructuring with a debt reduction was recorded, and does not capture the other unlikeliness-to-pay triggers. On the overlap year 2016, the approximated flag identifies 97.6% of the register defaults and produces a default rate that is 2.4% lower in relative terms than the register flag, with the difference concentrated in corporate unlikeliness-to-pay defaults. The effect is recorded as data deficiency DD-09-01; because the 2015 reference dates represent 9% of the calibration observations, re-running the threshold calibration without them changes no selected threshold.

sections.heading: Automatic unlikeliness-to-pay triggers
sections.text: The following unlikeliness-to-pay triggers lead to default automatically and are mapped to source fields in the default engine: non-accrued status (NONACCR_IND in the general ledger interface), a specific credit risk adjustment or Stage 3 classification resulting from a significant perceived decline in credit quality, a sale of credit obligations at a credit-related economic loss above 5%, a distressed restructuring with a diminished financial obligation above 1%, bankruptcy or similar protection, and a forced sale of collateral. Exposures classified as credit-impaired (Stage 3) are considered defaulted in all cases, because the Bank does not apply the payment-delay exceptions of paragraph 39 of EBA/GL/2016/07. Collective allowances for incurred-but-not-reported losses and Stage 1 and Stage 2 allowances are not treated as indications of unlikeliness to pay. The credit-related economic loss on a sale is computed as L = (E − P)/E with a threshold of 5%, and the reasons for each sale and its loss are analysed by Financial Restructuring and Recovery before a loss is treated as not credit-related. Where a sale at a material credit-related loss precedes default identification, the date of sale is the date of default. The diminished financial obligation is calculated as (NPV0 − NPV1)/NPV0, with both net present values discounted at the original effective interest rate.

sections.heading: Case-by-case indicators and external information
sections.text: Additional unlikeliness-to-pay indicators defined per exposure type in CR-STD-110 §6.2, such as fraud, a significant decline in income or cash flow, covenant breaches and multiple forbearance, lead to a case-by-case assessment completed by Credit Risk Management within 30 days of detection. Each trigger and indicator is mapped to source-system fields in the UTP mapping table utp_map_v7.csv, and the outcome of every case-by-case assessment is recorded with its rationale in the credit workflow system CWS. For each indicator, the mapping table defines the identification method, the internal and external information sources and the monitoring frequency; external sources include the BKR credit register for retail obligors, the Central Insolvency Register and press and analyst monitoring for corporate obligors. Manual identification processes (watchlist reviews, forbearance lists and external insolvency alerts) are updated at least weekly, and daily for insolvency alerts. UTP triggers and dpd triggers are applied consistently across the Bank, the consumer credit subsidiary and the Belgian branch.

sections.heading: Forbearance and forborne exposures
sections.text: Forbearance flags are taken from the Forbearance Register (FBR) maintained by Credit Risk Management under the definitions of Annex V of Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/451. For every forbearance measure the diminished financial obligation is computed, and forborne exposures below the 1% threshold are assessed for other indications of unlikeliness to pay, including a large final lump-sum payment, a back-loaded or irregular schedule, a significant grace period and repeated forbearance. All exposures classified as forborne non-performing are classified as defaulted, and a quarterly control by Credit Risk Management verifies this and reviews forborne performing exposures for indications of unlikeliness to pay. Forborne performing exposures carry the flag FORB_PERF_IND and the forborne-performing probation end date FORB_PROB_END_DT, which the staging engine uses to keep these exposures in Stage 2 for at least the two-year probation period. Where the schedule is changed as a forbearance measure, the assessment of distressed restructuring is performed before days past due are counted on the modified schedule.

sections.heading: Technical past due
sections.text: Technical past due situations are recognised only in the cases listed in EBA/GL/2016/07, namely errors of the Bank's data or systems, failures of payment execution, time lags in the allocation of payments and the specified factoring cases; wrong credit decisions are never treated as technical past due. Each case is registered in the technical past due log with the IT incident number, corrected within 30 days and reviewed quarterly by Credit Risk Management. Between 2016 and 2025 the log contains 1,184 technical past due cases, of which 1,102 related to the 2019 migration of the consumer credit subsidiary; the corresponding default flags were corrected in the source systems before the RDS snapshot. Technical past due cases do not reset the staging backstop counter used for the 30 days past due criterion, which is based on the same materiality-adjusted counter as the default definition.

sections.heading: Default flag reconciliation and default definition register
sections.text: The default flag constructed in STG-RDS v3.0 was reconciled with the production default register of CR-STD-110 for all reference dates from 31 March 2016 onwards: 99.94% of obligor-level default events agree on flag and date, and the 181 differences are explained by retroactive corrections of default dates in the register after the RDS snapshot. The RDS default flag is constructed in accordance with CR-STD-110, including the materiality thresholds, the unlikeliness-to-pay triggers, the probation periods and the merging of multiple defaults. The default flags used for IRB and IFRS 9 purposes are reconciled quarterly between the risk data warehouse and the Finance Risk Data Platform (FRDP); the reconciliation of 31 December 2026 showed no unexplained difference. Credit Risk Management maintains the register of current and past default definitions, which records for each definition its scope, approving body and date, implementation date and a description of the changes; the register entry DoD-2021-01 records the implementation of EBA/GL/2016/07 and the ECB materiality threshold on 31 December 2020. The accounting definition of default used for Stage 3 is therefore guided by Article 178 CRR and covers both unlikeliness to pay and 90 days past due, with unlikeliness to pay identified before 90 days past due is reached where the triggers of section 3.4 apply.

sections.heading: Source systems and extraction
sections.text: STG-RDS v3.0 is built from monthly snapshots of the Finance Risk Data Platform (FRDP), which is the authoritative source for IFRS 9 input data and is fed by the mortgage administration HYPO-NL, the consumer lending platform CONS-CORE, the Corporate Loan System (CLS), the Arrears Management System (AMS), the Forbearance Register (FBR), the Early Warning and Watchlist system (EWS), the default engine and the IFRS 9 PD term structure store. Snapshots are extracted on the fifth business day after each quarter end, and the source snapshot reference dates of all 44 quarters are listed in section 8. The data set is mapped to the data domains Retail Lending, Corporate Lending, Credit Risk Management and Finance, each of which has one Data Owner recorded in the Group Data Catalogue. The IFRS 9 PD term structures used for the SICR ratio are produced by the IFRS 9 PD models for mortgages (MDL-07), corporates (MDL-08), consumer lending and retail SME, conditional on the macroeconomic scenarios and weights of MDL-10. No third-party data enter the RDS except the BKR registration status, whose lineage starts at the monthly BKR delivery received by the Bank and records the provider, the data product BKR-Toetsing and the delivery date.

sections.heading: Lineage and critical data elements
sections.text: The lineage of every RDS variable, including discarded variables used to construct retained variables, is documented in Annex A and in the Group Data Catalogue, and identifies the source system and fields, each intermediate data store, every transformation, filter, join and aggregation with the reference to the build script or ETL job, and the extraction frequency and timing. Every staging input variable and every data element used to construct the default target (default flag, default date, probation status) is designated as a critical data element; STG-RDS v3.0 contains 23 critical data elements. Each critical data element has a business definition, a technical definition and at least one data quality rule per applicable dimension, recorded in the DQ rule book DQR-STG-v3. The model owner agreed the data quality expectations for the 23 critical data elements with the Data Owners of the four domains in the data sharing agreement DSA-IFRS9-004 of 12 January 2027. Roles for the ownership and quality of the data are defined for business (Data Owners and Data Stewards in Finance and Credit Risk Management) and IT (FRDP platform owner in Finance Risk IT).

sections.heading: Exclusions
sections.text: Six exclusions are applied to the calibration population; none of them removes facilities from production stage allocation. E1 dormant facilities with zero balance and zero available limit: 2.1% of facility-quarters, no default events; E2 POCI assets: 0.02% of observations and 212 default events, excluded because they are not staged; E3 facilities in default at the reference date: 1.6% of observations, excluded because they are not in the performing population. E4 facilities without origination PD and without a feasible proxy: 0.4% of observations and 0.5% of default events; E5 intra-group positions: 0.1% of observations; E6 duplicate facility records created by the 2019 migration of the consumer credit subsidiary: 0.3% of observations, removed under the uniqueness rule. Each exclusion is justified, quantified by number of facilities, share of observations and number of default events, and assessed for its effect on representativeness in section 5.3, which concludes that no exclusion changes the default rate of any portfolio by more than 0.02 percentage points. Exclusion E1 exceeds 5% of observations in the consumer lending segment (6.8%, dormant credit cards) and was approved by the model owner on 26 February 2027 and reported to Model Validation.

sections.heading: Missing values and outliers
sections.text: Missing values are treated per variable as documented in Annex C, distinguishing values missing at random, values missing for a structural reason and values missing because of a data deficiency. The watchlist status is structurally missing for retail obligors outside the scope of the watchlist and is set to "not on watchlist"; missing days past due (0.02% of observations) are recomputed from the daily AMS history, so that no value is imputed statistically. Missing origination PDs of legacy facilities are replaced by the proxy of section 4.4, a documented and reproducible method; the share of proxied values is 14.8% for mortgages, 9.6% for retail SME and 3.1% for corporates, and the effect on the calibrated thresholds is assessed in MDD section 7.5. Outliers of the SICR ratio above 50, caused by the origination PD floor of 0.03%, are identified by a documented rule that is applied identically in the RDS build and the production engine; the ratio is capped at 50 for calibration statistics only, which has no effect on stage allocation because every relative threshold lies below 3.0. Missing values and outliers of the default flag and default date are not imputed; the 38 affected default events were investigated and corrected at source in the default register.

sections.heading: Origination PD and legacy proxy
sections.text: The origination PD term structure, the origination rating and the date of initial recognition are stored for every facility in the FRDP table ORIG_RISK for the full life of the facility and are never overwritten by later recalibrations. For loan commitments and financial guarantee contracts, the date of initial recognition is the date on which the Bank became party to the irrevocable commitment, and the origination PD is stored at that date. For modified financial assets that are not derecognised, ORIG_RISK retains the origination PD of the original, unmodified terms, while a modification with derecognition creates a new facility with a new date of initial recognition. For facilities originated before origination PDs were stored (mortgages before 2008, retail SME before 2012 and corporates before 2010), the origination PD is proxied by the PD of the earliest archived rating, adjusted to the origination date with the portfolio-average rating migration between origination and first rating; the proxy approach is documented as EJ-09-03 and data deficiency DD-09-02. For mortgages, allocating legacy facilities with the alternative proxy (earliest rating without migration adjustment) changes the Stage 2 share of legacy facilities from 7.1% to 7.6%, and the impact on the total loss allowance is EUR 1.9 million.

sections.heading: Staging input variables
sections.text: The staging engine uses days past due at facility level, based on the same materiality-adjusted counter as the definition of default, the forborne performing flag and probation end date from FBR, and the watchlist status from EWS, in addition to the current and origination lifetime PD term structures. The watchlist status is maintained by Credit Risk Management under CR-POL-001 §10.1, whereby obligors triggering an early-warning indicator are assessed within 30 days and placed on the watchlist where deterioration is confirmed; performing exposures of obligors on the watchlist are allocated to Stage 2. Performing exposures more than 30 days past due on a material amount are allocated to Stage 2, and the rebuttable presumption of IFRS 9 is not rebutted for any portfolio. The RDS contains these inputs at each reference date so that the full stage allocation, not only the quantitative criterion, can be replicated and back-tested. The facility grouping variables (portfolio, product, origination PD band, collateral type, origination vintage and remaining term) are stored with each observation so that collective assessment and performance analysis can be performed on groups sharing credit risk characteristics.

sections.heading: Data ownership, metadata and change control
sections.text: Metadata for every RDS variable (business and technical definition, type and format, permitted values, unit and currency, source, Data Owner, update frequency and classification) are recorded in the Group Data Catalogue, using the integrated group taxonomy with the global customer identifier GCID and the facility identifier FAC_ID. The accounting and prudential notions of default are identical under FIN-STD-200 §4.2, but the credit-impaired flag used for Stage 3 (IFRS9_CI_IND) and the prudential default flag (DOD_FLAG) are labelled distinctly and their identity is verified by the quarterly reconciliation of section 3.5. Metadata changes are versioned in the catalogue so that the definition applicable to any historical data point can be retrieved. Changes to the definition, source or transformation logic of a staging input are approved by the Data Owner and announced to the model owner through the FRDP change calendar at least one quarter before implementation. The lineage documentation is updated before changed data are used in development, monitoring or production; the change of the watchlist feed from monthly to daily in March 2026 was reflected in lineage version 3.2 before its first production use.

sections.heading: Manual interventions
sections.text: The RDS build and the production data flow are fully automated, and no manual data manipulation is used in the build; the two unavoidable manual inputs, the legacy product mapping table map_cons_legacy_v4.csv and the UTP mapping table utp_map_v7.csv, are version-controlled files documented as expert judgement EJ-09-03 and as a Credit Risk Management reference table respectively. Manual interventions in the production flow are limited to stage overrides entered in the Staging Override Tool and to the collective Stage 2 transfer list maintained by IFRS 9 Modelling; both are identified in the lineage together with their controls (four-eyes approval in the tool and reconciliation of the transfer list to the Group Impairment Committee decision). Corrections of model data not supported by source evidence are not permitted; the 38 corrections of default dates referred to in section 4.3 were made at source with documented evidence.

sections.heading: Representativeness
sections.text: The representativeness of STG-RDS v3.0 for the portfolio at 31 December 2026 was assessed on the distributions of the staging drivers and on default-rate levels, with the detailed tables in Annex B. The population stability index of the origination PD band distribution between the last calibration year (2025) and the portfolio at 31 December 2026 is 0.03 for mortgages, 0.07 for consumer lending, 0.04 for retail SME and 0.05 for corporates, and the PSI of the SICR ratio distribution lies between 0.04 and 0.08. Observed one-year default rates in 2026 (mortgages 0.29%, consumer lending 1.84%, retail SME 1.60%, corporates 0.39%) lie within the range observed in the calibration window for every portfolio. Qualitatively, the product mix, the underwriting standards and the arrears and collection processes are unchanged except for the consumer credit card limit policy tightened in 2024, which reduces the share of high origination PD facilities. It is concluded that STG-RDS v3.0 is representative of the current portfolio for the purpose of threshold calibration.

sections.heading: Representativeness for other uses
sections.text: The staging model is applied to financial institutions, sovereigns and debt securities, which are not represented in the calibration population because of their very low number of defaults. For these exposures the corporate thresholds are applied, and debt securities with an internal rating equivalent to investment grade use the low credit risk exemption described in MDD section 4.8; the internal rating is primary, and where it is more favourable than the external rating the difference is justified in the credit file. The representativeness of the corporate thresholds for these exposures is assessed qualitatively by comparing the PD ranges: 98% of these exposures have origination PDs within the range covered by the corporate calibration population. This use is recorded as limitation LIM-09-10 in the MDD.

sections.heading: Impact of exclusions
sections.text: The effect of each exclusion on the distribution of origination PD bands and on default rates was quantified by comparing the calibration population with and without the exclusion. Exclusion E4 (no origination PD and no feasible proxy) has the largest effect, reducing the consumer lending default rate by 0.02 percentage points because the affected facilities are concentrated in pre-2012 overdrafts; all other exclusions change default rates by less than 0.01 percentage points. Re-running the threshold calibration with E4 facilities included at the portfolio-average origination PD of their product changes no selected threshold. The exclusions therefore do not bias the calibration, and the data remain complete for the purpose of ECL measurement because excluded facilities continue to be staged in production.

sections.heading: Data quality assessment
sections.text: A documented data quality assessment of STG-RDS v3.0 was performed before the recalibration, against the mandatory dimensions completeness, accuracy, consistency and timeliness and the additional dimensions validity, uniqueness and appropriateness of MRM-STD-022; the results per critical data element are reported in the data quality assessment report EVD-09-DQ. All 23 critical data elements are green on completeness (99.4% to 100% non-missing after structural missing values), and the reconciliation of the gross carrying amount to the general ledger at the four 2025 quarter ends shows differences between 0.03% and 0.08%. Two consistency rules were amber during 2019 (migration of the consumer credit subsidiary) and are explained by data deficiency DD-09-03. The assessment concluded that the data are fit for the calibration and back-testing of the SICR thresholds, and was signed off by the model developer R. Jansen and the model owner E. van Dijk on 26 February 2027 before the RDS was frozen.

sections.heading: Data deficiencies
sections.text: The data deficiency log of MDL-09 contains five open deficiencies, each with affected variables and segments, data quality dimension, cause, estimated impact, treatment, owner and target date. DD-09-01 approximated default flag for 2015 (consistency; impact −2.4% on the 2016 overlap default rate; treatment: methodological, sensitivity; cross-reference LIM-09-03). DD-09-02 missing origination PD for legacy facilities (completeness; 14.8% of mortgages, 9.6% of retail SME; treatment: proxy under EJ-09-03; cross-reference LIM-09-04). DD-09-03 incomplete forbearance history of the consumer credit subsidiary before May 2019 (completeness; 0.9% of consumer observations; treatment: exclusion from the forbearance backstop analysis; cross-reference LIM-09-05). DD-09-04 monthly instead of daily watchlist history for retail SME before 2017 (timeliness; treatment: accepted, no remediation possible; cross-reference LIM-09-09) and DD-09-05 muted arrears signal during the 2020 payment moratoria (accuracy of the staging signal; treatment: exclusion from the calibration objective under EJ-09-04; cross-reference LIM-09-06). Each deficiency is also recorded in the Bank data issue register (DIR-2027-0112 to DIR-2027-0116); DD-09-03 was remediated at source in 2019 for new data, and none of the deficiencies is rated high or critical, so no escalation to the Group Data Governance Committee was required.

sections.heading: Data quality thresholds
sections.text: The DQ rules for the critical data elements use the default amber and red thresholds of MRM-STD-022 §4.3, except for the default flag, the default date and days past due, for which stricter thresholds apply (amber below 99.5% and red below 99.0% on consistency, and amber above 0.1% and red above 0.25% on reconciliation differences). No threshold is less strict than the defaults, so no deviation required approval under MRM-STD-022 §4.5; the stricter thresholds were approved by the model owner together with this document. The DQ rules are documented in the DQ rule book DQR-STG-v3, and the 41 recurring checks are implemented in the Group DQ monitoring tool with a monthly run on the production input data. Red threshold breaches on a critical data element of the staging model are escalated to Model Risk Management within ten business days and reported to the Model Risk Committee.

sections.heading: Data quality of production input data
sections.text: The DQ rules applied to STG-RDS v3.0 are applied unchanged to the monthly production input data of the staging engine, so that production data quality can be compared with the development data. Production runs are blocked when the completeness check on current PDs, days past due or default flags is red, and the fallback rule then allocates facilities without a current PD to Stage 2 until the data are corrected. The input data are reconciled to the general ledger at each quarterly reporting date, and the gross carrying amount difference at 31 December 2026 was 0.04%, below the Finance materiality threshold. The staging output is available on the third business day after month end, which meets the Finance closing timetable for quarterly and monthly reporting; during the 2020 stress period the same timetable was met.

sections.heading: Lawful basis and purposes
sections.text: The staging model processes personal data of natural persons (retail mortgage and consumer lending customers and sole proprietors in retail SME) for three purposes recorded in the Record of Processing: calibration and development, independent validation, and monthly production stage allocation for financial reporting. Production stage allocation is based on Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR, the legal obligation to prepare financial statements under the IAS Regulation (EC) No 1606/2002 and Book 2 of the Dutch Civil Code, and development and validation are based on Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR, with the legitimate interest assessment LIA-2024-033 documenting purpose, necessity and the balancing against data subjects' rights. The lawful bases were recorded before processing started, in the Record of Processing entry ROPA-FIN-0147 of 11 March 2024. The reuse of loan administration data, collected for contract execution, for model development was assessed as compatible under Art. 6(4) GDPR in the compatibility assessment CA-2024-019, which considers the link between purposes, the context of collection, the nature of the data, the possible consequences for data subjects and the pseudonymisation applied. Processing is transparent to customers through the Bank's privacy statement, which lists regulatory reporting and risk model development as processing purposes.

sections.heading: Data minimisation, pseudonymisation and security
sections.text: STG-RDS v3.0 contains the following personal data attributes: pseudonymised obligor token, facility identifier, product and origination date, contractual maturity, gross carrying amount and limit, PD term structures, days past due and arrears amount, forbearance flag and reason category, watchlist status and default flag and date; each attribute is justified by its role in stage allocation or in the calibration target in Annex A. Name, address, date of birth, postcode, income and nationality are not extracted, so that personal data use is limited to what is necessary for stage allocation. Direct identifiers are replaced by keyed HMAC-SHA256 tokens in the FRDP extraction layer, with the keys held by the Group Data Office as separate data custodian; re-identification is possible only for a Privacy Office-approved purpose and is logged, and no re-identification took place for this RDS. The RDS is held only in the secure analytics environment SAE-RISK with role-based access for the eleven named members of IFRS 9 Modelling and Model Validation, encryption at rest and access logging. Implementation testing uses the pseudonymised RDS extract, not identifiable production data.

sections.heading: Protected attributes and fair treatment
sections.text: No protected attributes (such as gender, ethnic origin, nationality or religion) and no age variable are used in the staging model or its calibration. Special categories of personal data are not processed: the forbearance reason code "illness or disability" in FBR is mapped to the generic category "income loss" in the extraction layer, so that no health data enter the RDS. The staging inputs are PDs, arrears, forbearance and watchlist status; proxy screening against postcode-level and age-related information, performed for the IFRS 9 PD models, found no staging input that acts as a proxy for a protected attribute, and the results are documented in the RDS documentation of those PD models and summarised here.
