sections.heading: Monitoring plan and KPIs
sections.text: The monitoring plan MP-09 v3.0, approved by the model owner on 21 May 2027 and reviewed by Model Validation on 10 May 2027, is part of this chapter. Monitoring is performed quarterly, which exceeds the semi-annual minimum for Tier 2 models, and results are finalised within 45 calendar days after the quarter end. The KPIs, computed for the whole model and for each portfolio and origination PD band, are: K1 capture rate (green from 60%, amber from 45%, red below 45%); K2 Stage 1 direct-to-default share (green up to 25%, red above 35%); K3 backstop-only share (green up to 15%, red above 25%); K4 stage reversal rate (green up to 25%, red above 35%); K5 PSI of the SICR ratio and of the origination PD band distribution (0.10/0.25); K6 coverage (share of facilities with fallback allocation or proxied origination PD, green below 0.5% fallback); K7 stage override rate (green up to 2%, red above 5%); K8 production DQ results; and K9 overlays and collective transfers in place. The KPIs were set because MV-HB-003 does not define staging-specific tests; they measure discriminatory power, stability, data quality, overrides, overlays and coverage. The plan is updated whenever the model changes and reviewed at least annually; version 3.0 adds the band-level K1 reporting.

sections.heading: Escalation and reporting
sections.text: Each amber KPI is analysed by the model owner and its cause documented in the monitoring report; a red result, or amber on the same KPI in two consecutive quarters, is notified to MRM and Model Validation within ten business days, followed by a root cause analysis and action plan within 60 calendar days. The action plan proposes no action with justification, a temporary overlay, recalibration, redevelopment or a restriction of use, and changes are processed under MRM-STD-050. A red outcome is also assessed against FIN-STD-200 §12.3, requiring a remediation plan approved by the Model Risk Committee within three months and an assessment of the need for a temporary overlay. The quarterly monitoring report shows each KPI with value, threshold, traffic light and trend over the last four quarters, the override rates by direction, reason and approving unit, the overlays in place with amount and planned removal date, and model coverage. The report is sent to Finance and to Credit Risk Management; monitoring code and data are version-controlled in ifrs9/stg-monitoring so that results are reproducible.

sections.heading: Materiality, challenge and approval
sections.text: Each judgement is classified by its impact on the loss allowance and on the share of exposures changing stage relative to the output without the judgement or the best statistical alternative; EJ-09-01, EJ-09-02, EJ-09-05 and EJ-09-06 are medium materiality and EJ-09-03 and EJ-09-04 low. Medium judgements were approved by the model owner and the Head of Credit Risk Modelling, low judgements by the model owner, and no proposer approved his or her own judgement. Every medium judgement was challenged before approval by K. Hendriks of Retail Credit Risk Modelling, who is independent of the proposers, and the challenge and its resolution are recorded in the log; the knee-point rule was, for example, challenged against a fixed capture-rate target. No judgement is unquantifiable, and the aggregate effect of all judgements is an increase of the loss allowance by EUR 24.6 million (1.6%) and of the Stage 2 share by 1.8 percentage points against the best statistical alternative, below the high-materiality threshold, so no MRC approval of the aggregate was required. All judgements were reviewed at the 2026 annual review; EJ-09-07 (energy-intensive sectors) was withdrawn with CST-2022-02 and remains in the log as withdrawn.

No judgement is unquantifiable, and the aggregate effect of all judgements is an increase of the loss allowance by EUR 24.6 million (1.6%) and of the Stage 2 share by 1.8 percentage points against the best statistical alternative, below the high-materiality threshold, so no MRC approval of the aggregate was required.
All judgements were reviewed at the 2026 annual review; EJ-09-07 (energy-intensive sectors) was withdrawn with CST-2022-02 and remains in the log as withdrawn.

sections.heading: Stage overrides and management overlays
sections.text: Manual stage overrides are permitted only under the staging override policy in IS-09, which specifies the permitted reasons (SO-01 information on financial difficulty not yet reflected in PD or watchlist, SO-02 sector or regional deterioration identified by Credit Risk Management, SO-03 correction of a documented data error), a maximum change of one stage, the required evidence and the authority levels. Overrides to a lower stage are allowed only under SO-03 with an IT incident reference. Each override records the reason code, a written rationale, the supporting evidence, the proposer and the approver in the Staging Override Tool, and is approved by a credit officer of Credit Risk Management independent of the proposer. Override rates, direction and magnitude are monitored quarterly by portfolio, reason and approving unit under K7. Overlay OVL-2025-02 addresses the specific limitation LIM-09-02, is quantified by an alternative model run applying lifetime ECL with a stressed refinancing PD, and has a remediation plan to integrate an interest-only maturity criterion in model version 2.3 by 31 December 2027. The overlay is recorded in the overlay register with its rationale, the limitation addressed, the affected portfolio and stages, the quantification method, amount, approval and review date, was approved by the Group Impairment Committee on 27 March 2025 after review by Model Validation, and is reassessed quarterly. Because the overlay has been in place for more than four consecutive quarters, the model change assessment MCA-2026-007 under MRM-STD-050 was opened on 10 February 2026.

documents.title: Data quality assessment report – STG-RDS v3.0 and staging production inputs

sections.heading: Scope and approach
sections.text: This report documents the data quality assessment of STG-RDS v3.0 performed before the recalibration of the staging thresholds for model version 2.2, and the comparison with the data quality of the monthly production input data of the staging engine in 2026. The assessment covers the 23 critical data elements of the model against the mandatory dimensions completeness, accuracy, consistency and timeliness and against validity, uniqueness and appropriateness, applying the 41 rules of the DQ rule book DQR-STG-v3. The rules were defined jointly by the model developer and the Data Stewards of the Retail Lending, Corporate Lending, Credit Risk Management and Finance domains. For every critical data element at least one rule is defined per applicable mandatory dimension; timeliness is recorded as not applicable to static origination attributes, with the reason stated in the rule book. Controls over the staging input data are designed to be as robust as those over accounting data, since the gross carrying amount and the stage flag feed the general ledger postings of the loss allowance.

sections.heading: Completeness
sections.text: Completeness was measured at record level by reconciling the number of facilities per reference date and portfolio with the FRDP facility register, and at attribute level as the share of non-missing values per variable. Record-level completeness is 100% for all 44 reference dates after the documented exclusions, and all in-scope obligors, facilities and default events are included. Attribute-level completeness ranges from 99.4% (FORB_REASON) to 100% (GCA, DOD_FLAG, DEFAULT_DATE) after structural missing values; PD_LT_ORIG is 88.4% complete before and 99.6% after the legacy proxy, and the gap is recorded as DD-09-02. The incomplete forbearance history of the consumer credit subsidiary before May 2019 affects 0.9% of consumer observations; its impact on the forbearance backstop analysis was assessed as immaterial (DD-09-03).

sections.heading: Accuracy and reconciliation
sections.text: Accuracy was measured by reconciling the RDS to the general ledger and to the source systems for gross carrying amount, off-balance exposure and record counts per reference date. The gross carrying amount reconciles to the general ledger within 0.03% to 0.08% at every quarter end of 2023–2025, and record counts per reference date agree exactly with the FRDP facility register; the reconciliation differences are explained by accrued interest on off-balance positions booked on a different day. Critical data elements are reconciled against the source systems or accounting data at least annually; the 2026 reconciliation found no unexplained difference that required registration as a data quality issue. As a Tier 2 model, sample-based verification against source documentation is not required; nevertheless, 200 forbearance flags were verified against the credit files, with 199 confirmed and one corrected at source.

sections.heading: Consistency
sections.text: Consistency was assessed between the RDS and the production input data, over the observation period, including the change of default definition on 31 December 2020, and as logical consistency between related fields. Logical rules include: DOD_FLAG = 1 implies DEFAULT_DATE not null (100% passing), FORB_PERF_IND = 1 implies FORB_PROB_END_DT after the reference date (99.8%), DPD_MAT above 90 implies DOD_FLAG = 1 (99.97%, differences explained by technical past due cases), and GCA above zero or limit above zero (100% after exclusion E1). Two rules were amber in 2019 due to the migration of the consumer credit subsidiary and are green in all other years. The comparison of the 2025 RDS quarters with the 2026 production input data showed identical rule results within 0.1 percentage points for all rules.

sections.heading: Timeliness
sections.text: Timeliness is measured as the lag between the reference date and data availability and as the currency of periodically refreshed items. Days past due and default flags are available on the first business day after the reference date, PD term structures on the second business day and watchlist status on the first business day since the daily EWS feed of March 2026; before 2017 the retail SME watchlist history was available only monthly (DD-09-04). The currency of the behavioural PDs is monthly for retail and at most twelve months for non-retail ratings; 0.6% of corporate facilities had a rating older than twelve months at 31 December 2026 and were allocated through the fallback rule. Aggregated staging data are available within three business days after the reference date, which meets the reporting timetable.

sections.heading: Validity, uniqueness and appropriateness
sections.text: Validity rules check formats, types and permitted values (for example stage values 1 to 3, PDs between 0.0003 and 1, days past due non-negative); all validity rules are green with pass rates of at least 99.9%. The uniqueness rule on facility and reference date identified 266,000 duplicate facility-quarters created by the 2019 migration, which are removed under exclusion E6. Appropriateness for the model's range of application is assessed in chapter 5 of the RDS documentation, which concludes that the data are representative of the current portfolio on driver distributions and default-rate levels. The data include all information relevant to staging, and no exclusion removes data in a way that could bias the SICR calibration.

documents.title: Change memorandum CHG-2027-031 – Recalibration of consumer lending SICR thresholds

sections.heading: Description and rationale
sections.text: The change recalibrates the relative SICR thresholds of the consumer lending portfolio from 2.5, 2.0 and 1.75 to 2.25, 1.9 and 1.6 for the three origination PD bands, and the absolute threshold from 1.00 to 0.75 percentage points, and adds band-level capture-rate reporting to the monitoring extract. The rationale is the amber capture rate of consumer lending in two consecutive quarters of 2026, caused by the shift of the portfolio towards lower origination PDs after the credit card limit policy change of 2024. The change was recorded in the change log of the model inventory on 9 April 2027, before implementation in production.

sections.heading: Classification
sections.text: The change is classified as internally non-material: it does not modify the methodology, the drivers, the default definition, the range of application or the use, and its output impact is below the thresholds of MRM-STD-050 §5.2(e). A regulatory classification (Class A, B or C) is not applicable, because the staging model does not require supervisory permission. The classification proposed by the model developer was reviewed and approved by MRM on 22 April 2027; there was no disagreement requiring escalation to the MRC. The classification was confirmed by comparison with the change of version 2.1, which had a similar scope and was also classified as non-material.

sections.heading: Quantitative impact
sections.text: At the most recent reference date, 31 December 2026, the change increases the total loss allowance by EUR 6.3 million (0.4%) and the consumer lending loss allowance by 3.1%, and changes the stage of 1.9% of consumer lending exposures and 0.1% of all exposures in scope. Both impacts are below the 5% output threshold and the 10% threshold on class assignments. The impact on the Stage 2 share of the gross carrying amount is +0.1 percentage points (from 9.4% to 9.5%).

sections.heading: Cumulative impact
sections.text: The cumulative impact of all changes since the last full validation (VR-2024-006), namely the consumer absolute threshold reduction in version 2.1 (EUR 4.8 million) and this change (EUR 6.3 million), is EUR 11.1 million or 0.7% of the loss allowance, with 3.4% of consumer lending exposures changing stage. The changes were not split or sequenced to avoid a higher classification: the version 2.1 change was triggered by the 2024 back-test and this change by the 2026 back-test. Taken together the non-material changes do not meet the criteria of §5.2, so the next periodic validation need not be full-scope on this ground.

sections.heading: Validation requirement
sections.text: As a non-material change to a Tier 2 model, the change does not require validation before implementation and will be reviewed at the next periodic validation due by September 2027. Model Validation was informed of the change memorandum on 10 April 2027 and did not request an earlier review. The change does not trigger a re-validation under MRM-STD-050 §6.4, because the monitoring outcome that prompted it was amber and not red, and the portfolio composition and intended use are unchanged.

sections.heading: Implementation plan and post-implementation review
sections.text: The change is implemented in ICE release 2.2.0 with a parallel run on the reporting date 31 March 2027 and go-live on the reporting date 30 June 2027. A post-implementation review comparing the realised with the estimated impact will be performed after two quarterly reporting dates and reported to MRM. The parallel run of 31 March 2027 confirmed the estimated impact: the loss allowance increased by EUR 6.1 million against the EUR 6.3 million estimated at 31 December 2026, and 1.9% of consumer lending exposures changed stage. The rollback plan restores the version 2.1 parameter file through the release register if the go-live reconciliation fails.

sections.heading: Approval and inventory update
sections.text: The change was approved by the model owner E. van Dijk on 23 April 2027, after MRM confirmed the non-material classification on 22 April 2027, and model version 2.2 was recorded in the model inventory on 22 April 2027. The model owner will update the inventory record for the go-live of release 2.2.0 within ten business days of the reporting date 30 June 2027, and the superseded threshold table of version 2.1 remains archived in the release register. The change memorandum, the parallel run results and MDD version 3.0 form the evidence package for the review of the change at the next periodic validation.

deficiencies.rationale: Overlay OVL-2025-02 (interest-only mortgages, EUR 11.8 million) has been in place since Q1 2025. The model change assessment MCA-2026-007 was opened in February 2026 but has not been concluded more than a year later, and the integration of an interest-only maturity criterion is only planned for model version 2.3.

mitigation.text: Conclude MCA-2026-007 with a classified change proposal, and set a dated plan to replace the collective transfer by a model criterion. Report progress to the Group Impairment Committee each quarter until the overlay is removed.

deficiencies.rationale: The 12-month PD proxy for revolving consumer facilities is supported by an agreement analysis for credit cards only (98.7%). No evidence is provided that the proxy is not materially different for overdrafts, whose balance dynamics differ.

mitigation.text: Extend the agreement analysis of MDD section 4.4 to overdrafts. If the difference is material, apply the lifetime comparison to them.

deficiencies.rationale: The annual review compares the 12-month default rate of overridden obligors with that of model-allocated Stage 2 obligors in aggregate only. The analysis by original and final stage, and for downward (SO-03) overrides, is missing.

mitigation.text: Add the override performance analysis by original and final stage and by override direction to monitoring plan MP-09 and to the next annual review.

deficiencies.rationale: The MDD documents relative thresholds that decrease with origination PD. Validation's band-level re-performance shows a problem for mortgages originated below 0.10% PD (38% of the lowest band). There, the absolute threshold of 0.20 percentage points always binds, so the effective relative threshold exceeds 4 and the capture rate of this sub-population is 38% against 72.8% for the portfolio. The intended dependence of significance on origination risk is therefore not achieved for the lowest-risk mortgages.

mitigation.text: Re-assess the interaction of the absolute and relative thresholds below 0.25% origination PD, for example with an origination-PD-dependent absolute threshold. Document the capture rate per sub-band.

deficiencies.rationale: The staging back-test reports a 59.5% share of defaults in Stage 2 at least six months before default. Validation found that 1,410 defaults on facilities derecognised and replaced within six months before default (refinancing, product switches) were excluded because no six-month stage history exists. Including them with the stage history of the predecessor facility lowers the capture rate to 56.7%.

mitigation.text: Link predecessor and successor facilities in the back-test population and restate the 2026 capture rates. Document the treatment of derecognised facilities in the monitoring plan.
